title: Types of rock
keyIdea: There are three main types of rock, named after how they form. Igneous rock forms when melted rock (magma underground or lava on the surface) cools and hardens; slow cooling makes big crystals. Sedimentary rock forms from layers of sand, mud or shells pressed together over a very long time, with the oldest layer usually at the bottom, and it is where fossils are found. Metamorphic rock is a rock that has been changed by heat and squeezing deep underground, without melting.
familyTip: Collect a few pebbles or look at a wall, a gravestone or a kitchen worktop. Ask: can you see crystals (igneous, like granite), grains or layers (sedimentary, like sandstone), or swirls and thin sheets (metamorphic, like marble or slate)? Build sandwich layers of bread and spreads and ask which layer went on first.

visual.caption: How did it form? Drag each rock, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: press layers into rock, decide where melted rock cooled, heat and squeeze rocks without melting, sort rocks, check a robot.

kid: Rocks are not all the same. Scientists sort them into three types by how they were made: igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic.

Igneous rock was once melted rock. Deep down it is called magma, and when it comes out of a volcano it is lava. When it cools, it goes hard. Granite cooled slowly underground, so it has big crystals. Basalt cooled fast, so its crystals are tiny.

Sedimentary rock is made of layers. Sand, mud and shells sink to the bottom of the sea. More layers pile on top and press down for a very long time, until the grains stick into rock. The bottom layer is the oldest. Fossils are found in this rock.
Metamorphic rock was another rock first. Deep underground, heat and squeezing changed it, but it did not melt. Limestone turns into marble, and mudstone turns into slate.
adult: Ages 7 to 9. England's Year 3 science asks children to compare and group rocks by appearance and simple properties and to describe how fossils form when living things are trapped in rock. Key words: igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic, magma, lava, crystals, sediment, layers, fossil, heat, pressure.

Igneous rock forms from cooled magma or lava. Granite cooled slowly deep down, so its crystals are large. Basalt cooled fast at the surface, so its crystals are tiny, and pumice is full of gas holes. Sedimentary rock forms when sediment settles in layers and is pressed and cemented: sandstone, mudstone, limestone, and chalk made from tiny sea creatures. Younger layers lie on older ones. Metamorphic rock forms when heat and pressure change a rock while it stays solid: mudstone to slate, limestone to marble, sandstone to quartzite.

A common mistake is to think metamorphic rock is melted rock: if rock melts, it becomes magma and cools into igneous rock. Children also expect fossils in any rock, but heat destroys remains in igneous rock and usually squashes them in metamorphic rock. Many think the top layer is the oldest; ask which layer went down first.

In the lab your child drops sand, mud and shells into a sea, drags a weight down to press them into rock and taps the oldest layer, decides where granite, basalt and pumice cooled, drags a heat marker to change limestone, mudstone and sandstone without melting them, sorts six rock cards and checks a robot.

practice.prompt: A cliff has {a} layers of sedimentary rock. Counting from the bottom, which layer is the youngest?
practice.hint: New layers settle on top of older ones. The youngest is the last one laid down.
practice.explain: The top layer settled last, so the youngest is layer {a}, counting from the bottom. Layer 1 at the bottom is the oldest.

practice.prompt: Each layer of mud in a lake took about {a} years to settle. How many years did 2 layers take?
practice.hint: Two layers, each taking the same time. Double it.
practice.explain: {a} + {a} = {=2*a} years. Layers build up slowly, which is why sedimentary rock takes so long to form.

practice.prompt: Basalt formed when lava cooled on the surface. What type of rock is it?
practice.hint: Lava is melted rock. What do we call rock made when melted rock cools?
practice.explain: Rock made when lava or magma cools and hardens is igneous rock.

practice.prompt: Where would you look for a fossil?
practice.hint: Fossils form when a living thing is buried in mud or sand.
practice.explain: Plants and animals get buried in layers of mud or sand that slowly turn into sedimentary rock, so fossils are found there.

practice.prompt: Mudstone deep underground is heated and squeezed but does not melt. It becomes slate. What type of rock is slate?
practice.hint: It was another rock first, then it was changed.
practice.explain: Slate is metamorphic: mudstone changed by heat and squeezing, without melting.

pool.prompt: A rock face has {a} layers. Layer 1 is at the bottom. Which layer number is the oldest?
pool.hint: The first layer to settle is at the bottom.
pool.explain: Layer 1, at the bottom, settled first, so it is the oldest of all {a} layers.

pool.prompt: A rock collection has {a} granite pebbles and {a} basalt pebbles. How many igneous pebbles is that?
pool.hint: Granite and basalt are both igneous rocks. Add them.
pool.explain: Granite and basalt both formed from cooled melted rock, so all {=2*a} pebbles are igneous.

pool.prompt: Granite has big crystals. Where did it cool?
pool.hint: Big crystals need a long time to grow.
pool.explain: Magma deep underground cools slowly, so the crystals have time to grow big. That is granite.

pool.prompt: Chalk is made of tiny shells pressed together. What type of rock is it?
pool.hint: Shells that settle and get pressed together make which type?
pool.explain: Chalk is sedimentary: the shells of tiny sea creatures settled in layers and were pressed into rock.

pool.prompt: What happens to make metamorphic rock?
choices: A rock is heated and squeezed, but does not melt
pool.hint: Meta means change. The rock changes but stays solid.
pool.explain: Heat and squeezing deep underground change a rock without melting it. If it melted, it would cool into igneous rock.

pool.prompt: Limestone is heated and squeezed deep underground. What does it become?
pool.hint: It becomes a smooth, swirly metamorphic rock used for statues.
pool.explain: Heat and squeezing change limestone into marble, a metamorphic rock.

pool.prompt: Pumice is full of holes and can float. How did it form?
choices: Frothy lava with gas bubbles cooled fast
Layers of mud were pressed together
pool.hint: The holes were bubbles of gas in lava.
pool.explain: Pumice is igneous: frothy lava full of gas bubbles cooled so fast the bubbles were trapped.

pool.prompt: Which rock is made of sand grains stuck together in layers?
pool.hint: The name gives a clue: what is it made of?
pool.explain: Sandstone is sedimentary rock made of sand grains pressed and stuck together in layers.
